terms.comment: Lewis & Short has the adjective valētūdinārius; the neuter noun is in Celsus, Seneca and Tacitus.
Lewis & Short gives it with long ī (Greek νοσοκομεῖον).

phrases.latin: Hīc est valētūdinārium, ubi aegrōtī cūrantur.
phrases.english: This is the hospital, where sick people are looked after.

sources: Lewis & Short: valetudinarius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 174, 61, 64.
